title: Boots and Jet Pack
author: Claude
blurb: Two short levels about jumping again in the air. Kit's jump never runs out in the first, so a tap in the air lifts him again and he can tap his way up a cliff and across a gap, as if he wore a jet pack. In the second his boots hold only two jumps: each tap uses one, a third does nothing, and blue bubbles fill the boots up. Nothing here hurts. Signs explain each idea, and every level has a page on how it is made.

box.tagline: Tap again, and up you go.
box.back: A small explorer in a teal beanie has two levels to climb. In the first his jump never runs out, so a tap in the air lifts him again, up a tall cliff and across a gap. In the second his boots hold only two jumps, and blue bubbles fill them up. Signs say what each level shows, and the manual says how each is made.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
A jump with no limit is a jet pack; one with two uses is a pair of boots
Made to be copied and taken apart
